articleTitle: Torque Maximization Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Using a Two-Stage Virtual Signal Injection
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper proposes a new control scheme for torque maximization in permanent magnet synchronous motor drives. The proposed method is based on the extremum-seeking adaptive control and uses a two-stage virtual signal injection to improve efficiency under parameters uncertainty. The performance of the proposed method is compared with state-of-the-art methods using simulations.

articleTitle: A Model Predictive Control for a Multilevel Inverter Fed Induction Motor Drive Based on Three-Phase Triple Inverter Modular Topology
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Induction motor drives based on multilevel inverters have been established as a solution for many applications. Due to their interesting characteristics, several topologies have been proposed. One of the latest topologies is the one based on three-phase triple inverter modular topology. However, not much work has been realized regarding their control. Thus a field-oriented controller with a model predictive control (MPC) strategy to control this AC drive is proposed. The MPC will be used to control the AC currents of the inverter. One aspect that is inherent to this drive is the high number of voltage vectors. Thus, besides their predictive characteristic, this controller also shows their advantage dealing with this high number of voltage vectors. The capabilities of the proposed controller will be verified through a simulation study.

articleTitle: Temperature Gradient Improvement of Power Semiconductor Modules Cooled Using Forced Air Heat Sink
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper discusses the improvement of operational reliability and lifetime of power electronic modules due to the reduction of the temperature gradient in the semiconductor structures. High temperature gradient in the power electronic modules having a large area of the semiconductor structure is a more affecting issue than the junction temperature. The improvement in the temperature gradient is achieved by varying/degrading the thermal resistance along the heat sink length. A conventional cooling system for three semiconductor modules based on a forced air heat sink was modelled and analysed to derive a reduction rate of the appropriate thermal resistances. Implementation of the forced air heat sink having non-uniformed thermal resistances along the heat sink length ensures the uniform temperature distribution across the power semiconductors and, therefore, the improved thermal gradient.

articleTitle: Optimal Capacitor Placement and Sizing Using Constriction-Factor-Based Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper presents a two-step procedure to solve optimal capacitors placement and sizing in radial distribution and industrial power systems. In the first step, loss sensitivity index is investigated to identify the best candidates for capacitor installation. In the second step, a Constriction-Factor-Based particle swarm optimization is employed to identify the required level of reactive power compensation. The objective function consists of active power losses and capacitor costs while system constraints have to be fully achieved. The proposed procedure is applied to 85-bus radial distribution system and one real industrial power system. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed procedure to solve optimal capacitor placement and sizing problems improving the voltage profile, correcting power factor, and maximising savings due to active power losses.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Optimization of a Spoke-Type Ferrite Magnet Generator for Hydropower Plant Based on Metamodeling
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper presents the techno-economic metamodel-based optimization for different slot-pole combinations of a spoke-type interior permanent magnet synchronous generator. Optimization procedure and strategy were implemented in Ansys OptiSlang and Ansys Motor-CAD using MATLAB script. The novelty of the approach is reflected in the automatic three-line assessment of the demagnetization proximity implemented into the optimization procedure. Three slot-pole combinations, namely 135s30p, 144s24p i 144s30p, were optimized and compared based on generator active material cost and efficiency with the given optimization constraints.

articleTitle: A Novel FPGA HW Implementation for SVPWM Technique Using Taylor Series
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel Hardware implementation to perform Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation. Starting from the Taylor Series representation of the dwell-time equations for SVPWM technique and by managing opportunely the hardware resources of the digital controller, we obtained a novel hardware architecture of SVPWM technique that, unlike other the-state-of-art methods, avoids CORDIC core or Look Up Table-based approaches as well as further resources like Digital Signal Processor or external reference signals. The core of the architecture is an Arithmetic Logic Unit, which periodically perform all the calculation needed to obtain the value of the dwell-times, and permits to change in real time the output amplitude.The architecture is been implemented on an Xilinx Artix VII FPGA XC7A35T1CPG236C requiring 1973 LUTs and 501 Flip Flops, respectively the 9.49% and 1.2% of the overall resource, and a dynamic power consumption of 1.04 mW.

articleTitle: DC Magnetic Field Reduction Inside Particular Part of Space
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The attenuation of magnetic fields is important in many cases in order to protect living beings and electrical equipment from its harmful effect. This paper deals with the DC magnetic field reduction by shielding. A finite element method is applied to study the efficiency and reliability of various shield geometries, placed coaxially with a long current carrying wire, in order to decrease the magnetic field outside the shield. The impact of different combinations of permeability and thicknesses of applied ferromagnetic material is investigated. Calculating the shielding effectiveness, defined as the ratio of magnetic flux density magnitude without and with the shield, the most effective shields can be determined. The obtained results show that a partial shield can be good protection in many practical cases.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Modelling of an Eccentrically Loaded probe Coupled Cylindrical Cavity
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: In this paper, numerical Transmission Line-Matrix (TLM) method is applied to model an eccentrically loaded cylindrical cavity in order to analyze an impact of the eccentricity on the resonant frequency values. Two different types of meshes are considered, the structured, rectangular mesh and the unstructured, tetrahedral mesh and their possibilities and advantages are emphasized.

articleTitle: Robustness Analysis of Legendre Orthonormal Functions Based Model Predictive Control and PID Control of DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The paper presents robustness analysis of speed control of commonly used actuator, direct current (DC) motor. The paper presents results obtained when using model predictive control (MPC) controller based on Legendre orthonormal functions MPCL, and as other option, using proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. Performance was compared when there is mismatch in the model used for tuning, and the real system, the DC motor. Set of simulations were conducted and results are presented.

articleTitle: Determination of Initial Rotor Position of PMaSynRM Based on DC Current Injection
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The paper proposes the rotor parking procedure upgraded with actual rotor parking position error detection suitable for permanent magnet assisted synchronous motor drives. The approach is based on the well know DC current based rotor parking, but takes into account an expected parking position error due to the confrontation of the synchronous and the reluctant torque during the parking. The paper shows that the difference between the actual rotor parking position, and referent zero position of stator current vector, can be predicted and compensated by taking into account DC current level and motor parameters, with core saturation included.

articleTitle: Metamodel-based Design and Optimization of a Spoke-Type Interior Permanent Magnet Machine for a Vehicle Traction Application
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Interior permanent magnet machines are a popular solution for traction applications. Within the frame of this paper, an air-cooled spoke interior permanent magnet machine is designed and optimized with respect to the maximum average torque and minimum magnet mass. Several performance constraints, such as the permissible torque ripple and the relative thermal loading, have been considered in the design workflow. A metamodel, (or surrogate model) optimization is utilized with the help of Ansys OptiSLang tool. Within an initial sensitivity study, the metamodel predicts the optimal design space which shortens the cumulative optimization time from typical 1-2 weeks to approximately one day. It is shown that this simplification marginally reduces the solution accuracy (±4 %). The obtained Pareto front is verified using the finite element analysis through Ansys Motor-CAD proving that the selected optimized design meets all set requirements. The novelty of the proposed design is reflected in the combination of pole shaping strategy and rotor mass minimization by implementation of inter pole holes.

articleTitle: MAPT Control of PMaSynRM Including Magnetic Saturation
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The paper presents a Minimum Ampere per Torque control strategy for Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor. The algorithm aims to minimize the copper losses at any given torque level, and also results in maximum torque production for a given current limit. The suggested MAPT strategy takes into account the effects of magnetic saturation and gives optimal stator current vector using simplified recursive Newton-Raphson iterative method. The performances of the suggested optimal strategy were tested on the low voltage permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance drive intended for pump application.

articleTitle: Novel Approach for Estimating Slot Filling Factor in FEA Based Design of Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: A novel methodology is proposed for estimating the slot filling factor of random-wound single-layer and double-layer windings that can be easily included into Finite Element (FE) based design of electrical machines. Although several algorithms have been proposed in recent publications for maximizing slot filling factor of single-layer windings for a given conductor diameter and given slot geometry, no methodology for including these algorithms into machine design procedures has been proposed so far. Consequently, design of electrical machines, even if optimization is involved, is still often conducted under the assumption of empirically adopted constant value of the slot filling factor, resulting in suboptimal machine designs. This observation is especially relevant for metaheuristic electrical machine design optimization, where the slot geometry and number of turns per slot are constantly varied during optimization in order to maximize torque density or machine efficiency and where the assumption of constant slot filling factor is not justified. For this reason, a new approach for finding the optimal value of standard conductor diameter that yields maximum slot filling factor for each simulated machine is developed in this paper. Results of slot filling factor estimation by the developed procedure are presented for a Rotor Permanent Magnet Flux Switching (RPMFS) machine equipped with either a single-layer or a double-layer winding. It is demonstrated that the proposed approach maximizes torque density and minimizes losses for given dimensions of machine laminations, rated voltage, speed and torque.

articleTitle: Application of Filtration as a Measurement Method of Reactive Power Parameters
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Reactive power is one of the most important parameters of the signals of modern electrical power grids. In this case, the most informative parameters are the reactive power of the main spectral component and the reactive power of harmonics. To measure these parameters, there are lot of methods that are not highly accurate or difficult to implement. The paper discusses a new approach based on the application of a low-pass and band-pass filters to provide a phase shift equal to ±π/2. The basic principles of performing measurements by this approach are considered, analytical expressions are obtained for calculating the reactive power error. The case of application of a second-order low-pass filter and a second-order band-pass filter is considered in detail. The features of the application of this approach for the case of applying filters of a higher order are analyzed. Approaches are proposed to improve the measurement accuracy by additional measurement of the frequency or root mean square value (RMS) of the signal and adjusting the filter transfer coefficient. A method has been developed for calculating filter parameters in accordance with the required reactive power measurement error, the nominal frequency of the measured harmonic, the relative frequency deviation and the signal spectral composition.

articleTitle: Realization of a GSM Based Low Power Device for Measuring Environmental Parameters
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: Taking into account the increasing need for remote monitoring of various environmental parameters, there is also a growing necessity for small, independent, low power devices, which can measure the required data in real time and communicate it to the user. Practical realization of one such battery powered device is presented in this paper. It is comprised of a PCB that contains a microcontroller and a GSM modem as its main parts, three sensors which measure ambient temperature, illumination and ambient pressure, GSM antenna, battery, and a small solar panel. Main device functionality implies measuring of the three aforementioned physical quantities, their processing and sending to the user in a form of an SMS message via GSM network. Data can be sent periodically or following a user inquiry. The user also has an option of sending a few useful commands to the device in order to change some operational parameters. The main focus in realization of this device was to explore and test different operation modes of components used in order to minimize the power consumption as much as possible while maintaining the full necessary functionality. At the end, a comparison in total power consumption was done between the device running on two different firmware versions (with and without using power saving modes of components), which clearly shows the advantage in using these modes and gives a much better battery life and longer operating time.

articleTitle: A proposal of FH-SS synchronization with FPGA multichannel correlator implementation
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal for code synchronization for frequency agile systems based on the use of a real-time clock and a multi-channel digital correlator. The proposed synchronization scheme ensures reliability, short synchronization times and resistance to electronic interference and interception. In addition, a proposal for a multi-channel digital correlator has been developed and implemented for use in the synchronization scheme. This type of correlator is suitable for code synchronization in spread spectrum communication systems (DS-SS and FH-SS). The implemented correlator was later used to measure the false alarm probability and the detection probability of the code sequence. Finally, simulation and measurement results are summarized and presented graphically.

articleTitle: Winding Geometry Impact on High Power Medium Frequency Transformer Design
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: DC transformers make an essential building block in empowering future medium voltage direct current power distribution grids. To reach high efficiencies, the design of medium frequency transformers, one of the key elements of DC transformers, needs to be carried out, while fulfilling all technical requirements. The paper discusses the influence of the winding arrangement on the overall performance of a high power medium frequency transformer design. The particular influence is studied on a combination of nanocrystalline core material in a core-type transformer structure with various dispositions of hollow copper conductors as windings. The 2-vessel medium frequency transformer option proved to be the most efficient out of the three suggested ones and a prototype is made for the purpose of design verification.

articleTitle: Improved Control of Symmetrical Half-Bridge based Second-Order Harmonic Active Filters
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: DC systems connected to single-phase AC/DC converters are subject to a second-order harmonic ripple affecting the DC-bus voltage. Such ripple can be neutralized through an active filter circuit. This paper presents an improved control algorithm for a symmetrical half-bridge based active filter architecture. Contrarily to standard control approaches, the proposed solution does not require any external measurement other than the voltages and current internal to the active filter itself. This makes the analyzed active filter architecture suitable for a plug-and-play solution, meaning that it can be connected to the DC-bus terminals of a pre-existing system without any additional modification. The proposed control algorithm is based on multiple cascaded feedback loops, and the frequency and phase synchronization with the second-order harmonic component to be eliminated is based on an internally developed Phase-Locked-Loop (PLL). The developed approach has been numerically tested and validated in different operating conditions, showing satisfactory performances.

articleTitle: Cleanrooms pressure cascade: standard PID-based solutions and step forward to MIMO control
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: This paper gives in-depth analysis of the cleanrooms pressure cascade problem, where the starting point is the state-of-the-art control practice for stabilization and disturbance rejection of static pressure and air-flow rate. The plant components are modeled in order to obtain multivariable model of a typical plant in the context of heating-ventilation-air conditioning (HVAC) and variable-air-volume (VAV) based cascade control. Opposed to the standard control solutions realized by the independent PID loops, presented multivariable modelling enables the proper analysis and effective high-performance solutions of the control for the plants with observed strong internal couplings. The results and problems arising from the state-of-the-art control practice in pharmaceutical factories in the Republic of Serbia is given in a case study, and the open issues are highlighted.

articleTitle: Current THD comparison of different offset injections in the linear modulation range for cascaded H-bridge converters
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The equivalence of space vector pulse width modulation (PWM) and carrier-based PWM through the injection of a common-mode voltage is already known for two-level (first min-max injection) and multilevel (double min-max injection) three-phase converters. However, under regular sampled phase voltage references, these injections do not produce the lowest total harmonic distortion (THD) of the load phase current throughout the linear modulation index range. This paper proposes the use of a similar common-mode injection, called the second min-max injection that achieves the lowest current THD in regions of the modulation index range where the double min-max injection fails to do so. A cascaded H-bridge (CHB) topology is analyzed, and comparison is made between different multicarrier modulation strategies, using simulation results, under different injections for the whole modulation index range. The level-shifted in-phase disposition modulation method is found to produce the lowest load phase current THD with second min-max offset voltage injection for modulation indices below unity. For modulation indices greater than one, the double min-max injection is still considered as optimal.

articleTitle: Application of Chebyshev Polynomials to Estimate the RMS Measurement Error Caused by ADC Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: The ADC nonlinearity is one of the most significant sources of the measurement error of root mean square (RMS) digital measuring instruments. This is because the ADC nonlinearity effect on the final RMS error is difficult to compensate, especially in case of commercial instruments. To describe of ADC nonlinearity, there are a large number of techniques that characterizes some disadvantages, including an overestimation of the error estimate, the complexity of calculating of the error estimate, and the possibility of using only for certain ADC architectures. In this paper, we consider the application of Chebyshev polynomials to describe the ADC nonlinearity and the corresponding estimation of the RMS measurement error for this nonlinearity approximation approach. Analytical relationships have been obtained that make it possible to calculate the RMS measurement error. A method is proposed for assessing the ADC nonlinearity parameters by typical nonlinearity form for the case of considered approach of approximation. A qualitative comparison of the proposed approach with the existing ones (the "worst case" method, polynomial functions application, pseudorandom functions application) from the point of view of the error estimation accuracy and the complexity of error calculation is carried out. The influence of signal parameters and nonlinearity parameters on the RMS error is analyzed.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Two-Degrees-of-Freedom Current Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2022 XIV International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (INDEL)
abstract: A control scheme having two degrees of freedom is designed so that many issues such as disturbance and set-point response, model uncertainties and measurement noise are taken into account. For optimization of the disturbance performance a pole placement approach is combined with the minimization of the integrated error (IE). A feedforward compensator based on an inverse dynamic model of the plant gives the desired set-point response. Robustness is examined using the sensitivity function and the Nyquist plot. Design parameters are introduced allowing an engineer to trade-off between the conflicting objectives. Simulation results and experimental results of a current control loop are discussed. The proposed scheme is not limited to this application area.
